COVID ORPHANS

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The hidden South African pandemic: orphaned children who lost a promary or secondary caregiver due to Coronavirus. Here is how they have coped?

Unique Selling Point:
The cost of the COVID-19 pandemic is mostly noted in the people whose lives it has claimed— more than 89 000 deaths in SA, and more than 5 million worldwide. But there are the secondary victims, the collateral casualties— the children left orphaned. We investigate how they have been coping and question much-needed intervention from government and civil society.

Summary:
South Africa has the highest number of COVID-19 orphans on the continent. With more than 94 000 having lost parents and guardians on the past year. This was revealed in a study that found that more than 1.5 million children on the continent were orphaned after losing parents, guardians, caregivers during the pandemic. This was a multidisciplinary team of researchers from the oxford university in partnership with UCT.


Further information:
A study released this year found that South Africa recorded one of the highest numbers of primary caregiver deaths in the world. Between March 2020 to April this year, the study showed 82 422 children were orphaned and another 94 625 had lost their primary caregivers.

UCT, in partnership with the University of Oxford, conducted the research.

Co-author of the study, Professor Lucie Cluve said the found that one in every 200 South African children had lost a primary caregiver. Other countries with similar harrowing statistics include Peru, the US, India, Brazil and Mexico.

Press Release:


The COVID-19 pandemic has ravaged South African families, leaving a young generation facing a world without their parents. We explore what some experts call South Africa’s hidden COVID-19 pandemic, and question how thousands of young people orphaned by coronavirus are navigating their circumstances alone.

South Africa has the highest number of young people on the continent, orphaned by the coronavirus. With more than 94 000 having lost parents and guardians in the past year. We explore how the hidden pandemic of orphanhood will have a serious impact on children for generations to come.


Script:


AUDIO
VO – The COVID-19 pandemic has shattered the once tranquil lives of many families. It has been particularly unforgiving to older people with pre-existing medical conditions. In South Africa, COVID-19 has infected more than 2.9 million people with the official death toll at close to 90 000.Many of those who succumbed to their symptoms were caregivers and parents.


BILLY BADENHORST - CLIP 59 / DAY ONE FOLDER

08:09 At the beginning of this year, my father got sick with COVID...09:00 And not long after that, him and my mother, both, got so sick that they had to go to the hospital, wich was actually bad.


VO –25 year old Billy Badenhorst and his 14 year old brother Dewald were dealt a heavy blow when their parents,Billy Senior and Maliske, tested positive for Covid-19 in January 2021. Maliske’s condition deteriorated days after the couple was admitted.
BILLY BADENHORST - CLIP 59/DAY ONE FOLDER

9:36- ... my father called me and said she's not doing so well.Please bring her some stuff she likes...A day after that he called me crying. My father told me she just passed away.
VO – Heartbroken, and reeling from Covid-19 symptoms, Badenhorst's father discharged himself from the hospital.
BILLY BADENHORST - CLIP 59/DAY ONE FOLDER

09:51 He booked himself out of the hospital because he couldn't handle the pain and everything so he went home.
10:18 when we had the funeral, for my mother, he was so weak that he couldn't stand up and come to the funeral. We actually went there to try and help him to stand up but he just couldn't.


VO – The day after the funeral, Badenhorst got a phone call from his uncle, telling him to go home and check on his father.
BILLY BADENHORST - CLIP 59 /DAY ONE FOLDER

BILLY - 11:12 Then I just drove, I asked my boss, can I please go, I don’t think something is right.

11:23- ... When I got there he was just lying there on the ground. He was sitting basically. 11:41- ... he already passed away when I got there. bed.



VO – Badenhorst is now the primary caregiver for his epileptic brother. They’re both living in the home of Badenhorst’s girlfriend, Charnè, after their parents home was repossessed. But the Badenhorsts aren’t alone…
LINK – Over 3 million children are orphaned in South Africa and they need adoptive or foster care. Finding a good loving home has always been a challenge but the Covid-19 pandemic has exacerbated the problem in unprecedented ways.
VO – According to Professor Lucie Cluver, when a young child loses a parent or a caregiver, that child not only deals with heartache but also, with insecurity and doubts about the future.

PROF. LUCIE CLUVER - ZOOM FOLDER -

CLUVER - 01:18 - … I looked at the most recent data... and we see that already 135 000 children in South Africa have lost a parent to Covid-19.

BONGANI – 02:15 – So talk to us about the impact of watching a parent or caregiver get sick, then they die, and you're alone in the world and you're just a child?

CLUVER – 02:31 – This is something that many children in South Africa have already experienced, you know, we've been living with an HIV pandemic for many years now. … What we actually see is that the impacts of losing a parent are different for different ages. … We're also seeing in Covid-19 that around 65% of those orphans are teenagers. … And that is actually one of the most vulnerable times to lose a parent.
VO – Young people who have lost their caregivers to COVID-19 are lucky to be taken in by relatives, others are absorbed into the child welfare system while many are left to fend for themselves like Badenhorst and his brother.

16 year old Sandile Nxumalo, and her two other siblings, are being looked after by her aunt Edith after their mother, Ethel died in July.


SANDILE NXUMALO - CLIP 36 - DAY ONE

00:08 – She was someone who loved church. She's strict, talkative and loves laughing and her voice was loud. 00:28 -She loved helping people and she had dignity. She worked really hard.
VO – Sandile's mom died at the family home after she had been turned away from the hospital. Edith is concerned that the memory of seeing her mother lifeless, on the bed they once shared, will haunt Sandile for some time to come.


VO – Though her father is still alive, Sandile feels like an orphan because he has had no hand in her upbringing, making things harder for her aunt who has a child of her own.



EDITH NXUMALO - CLIP 43

08:34 - … It's not that easy. It's just a matter of, I think, love just keeps me going. I love them. so its easier, even if its that hard, I manage.

08:59 Some of the things I can't afford and then I'll try hard so that they don't feel the gap of not having the mom. I sacrifice even if I go into debt.

BONGANI LINK ON ORPHANS AND EMOTIONS.

VO – Professor Cluver says grief counselling is especially important for Covid orphans as death often strikes in a matter of days or weeks – leaving little time for a child to process a parent being ill, let alone dying.
PROF. LUCIE CLUVER - ZOOM FOLDER

BONGANI – 16:03 – What about behavioural changes for any child at whatever stage dealing with this level of loss?

CLUVER – 16:13 – Well, children's behaviour is often their way of expressing how they're feeling. There'll be so many times when you see a child who is shouting or screaming or hitting, and they are doing that because they are feeling desperately unhappy inside.
VO – The professor advocates for the integration of children into the extended family, as opposed to orphanages, but admits that that is not always an option.
PROF. LUCIE CLUVER

07:59 - … It can be a real challenge because the whole family and the child are reeling after a death and they have lost all their money. Sometimes a family falls apart and starts fighting after someone had passed away.
VO – Financial challenges may also mean that some families simply cannot afford to take in another member.
NATSOUND / BREAK – We need some natsound of the visuals we use to establish Chriselda so the move from the professor to Chriselda doesn't feel abrupt.
VO – It's a logical expectation that orphaned children who cannot be taken in by relatives, should be accommodated by child welfare services and linked to adoptive or foster parents.

But the pandemic has not spared guardians including responsible grandparents, adoptive and foster parents – many have also died. And so grieving children are hurled into the welfare system in need of new homes, explains Chriselda Bunu, from the Johannesburg Child Welfare.
CHRISELDA BUNU – JOHANNESBURG CHILD WELFARE SOCIETY - DAY TWO - CARD ONE

CHRISELDA - 08:41 - … It is extremely traumatic and remember, with most of our children, they have experienced the trauma of either having been abandoned, or having been removed from their family of origin and placed in foster care, and now they have built these relationships. The foster parent dies and now you have to move them again.

BONGANI – 12:14 – Generally, is the public open to fostering?

CHRISELDA - 12:14 – They are. There are challenges that are faced because there's a screening process. … which means then it makes it a delay for us to place children with foster parents because until we are sure that a person has been properly screened, we cannot place children with them.
VO – Even though the desire to adopt and foster children is clearly evident, the number of successful placements has decreased drastically.
CHRISELDA BUNU – JOHANNESBURG CHILD WELFARE SOCIETY - DAY TWO - CARD ONE

11:52 - … people are losing jobs, the economy, you know, so having to take on new mouths to feed – some people are reluctant to do that. … and we have more children we need to place.
.VO -Professor Cluver emphasizes that identifying and caring for children orphaned by Covid-19 should be a necessary and urgent aspect of government's response to the pandemic.


PROF. LUCIE CLUVER - ZOOM FOLDER

19:48 - … The first thing is that you keep a child in their family, ideally, or in a warm, loving foster family. The second thing is that you give the family financial support. … The third thing is that we need to make sure that that family gets parenting support. ...that they get support in how to support the child, but also, how to cope themselves.

NK – As bad as things seem now, the story of Covid has been one of so many unknowns. It's been a fast moving target and we're making up the rules as we go along. So with the number of orphans set to rise, there's no clear indication of how many people will be impacted in the long run and how much children will still suffer

VO – Badenhorst says taking care of Dewald is a huge responsibility but it's one that he is proud to execute, with the help of his girlfriend,

BILLY BADENHORST - CLIP 59

14:44 - … I've been doing my best as far as I can. I haven't been a parent, ever, so everything is new to me – 14:57 – schoolwork, taking him to school, making sure everything's okay and making sure his health is okay.
VO – And Sandile is also slowly adjusting to life without her mother.
PLEASE END THE PIECE WITH VISUALS OF SANDILE WALKING AWAY.
